insights.text: Two of the three ads lost roughly half their click-through rate over the seven weeks, but only one of them shows the pattern of fatigue. Autumn_Hero_A ran the same weekly impressions at an unchanged £4.00 CPM while weekly frequency climbed from 1.6 to 4.3, and its CTR fell from 1.10% to 0.511%. Fewer new people were seeing it each week and those already reached clicked less. Autumn_Lifestyle_C held its weekly CTR between 0.80% and 0.83% over the same weeks, which argues against a seasonal fall. A refreshed Hero execution, or a frequency cap near the early-flight level, is the response this evidence supports.

Autumn_Product_B's CTR fell almost as far, from 0.950% to 0.505%, but its weekly frequency stayed at 1.7 throughout, so the same people were not seeing it more often. What changed was delivery: weekly impressions rose from 700,000 to 1,204,000 on a near-flat budget as CPM fell from £5.00 to £3.03. The decline points to the ad being served into cheaper, lower-response inventory or a wider audience, not to the creative wearing out. A new execution is unlikely to recover it; the placement and audience breakdown for this ad by week would confirm where the extra impressions went.
alternatives_considered: audience broadening vs placement shift (cannot separate without breakdown)
